content.instructions: To perform a calculation, enter the required variables. Once all the inputs are entered, click the "Calculate" button to perform the calculation. Any time an input variable is adjusted, the "Calculate" button must be clicked to populate the new output. To start over, click the "Reset" button to clear all values and begin the calculation again. Traditionally, aminoglycoside antibiotics have been administered in multiple daily doses (aka, conventional dosing). An alternative approach to dosing these agents involves achieving higher peak concentrations and using an extended dosing interval. This strategy is often referred to as “extended interval dosing”, “single daily dosing”, or “once daily dosing”. The dosing interval is then adjusted based on a random level taken several hours after the end of the infusion using one of several interval adjustment nomograms. Certain limitations exist for each of the nomograms: Hartford Hospital nomogram: Only intended for use with gentamicin and tobramycin at a dose of 7 mg/kg. Random level must be drawn 6-16 hours after the start of infusion. University of Rochester Medical Center nomogram: Only intended for use with gentamicin and tobramycin at a dose of 5 mg/kg. Random level must be drawn 7-14 hours after the end of infusion. Urban-Craig (Gentamicin and Tobramycin) nomogram: Only intended for use with gentamicin and tobramycin at a dose of 5 mg/kg. Random level must be drawn 6-14 hours after the start of infusion. Urban-Craig (Amikacin) nomogram: Only intended for use with amikacin at a dose of 15 mg/kg. Random level must be drawn 6-14 hours after the start of infusion. If the level is undetectable and the patient is not showing signs of clinical response, conventional dosing should be considered.

general: The Urban-Craig nomogram requires a drug level that has been collected 6-14 hours after the start of infusion.
The University of Rochester Medical Center nomogram requires a drug level that has been collected 7-14 hours after the end of infusion.
The Hartford Hospital nomogram requires a drug level that has been collected 6-14 hours after the start of infusion.
